base_properties.human_readable: Legislature Retains Final Interpretive Authority (Parliamentary Sovereignty Reading)

perspectives.label: Rights Minorities Under Legislative Override
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 1: RIGHTS MINORITIES (SNARE) — Structurally vulnerable to majoritarian capture when legislature retains final interpretive authority. Cannot exit the jurisdiction; bear full cost of legislative override of established rights protections. No institutional counterweight when democratic mandate licenses fundamental rights restriction. Maximum extraction experienced by those whose constitutionally-protected interests conflict with legislative will.

perspectives.label: Judicial Branch
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 2: JUDICIAL BRANCH (TANGLED ROPE) — Experiences the constraint as a genuine coordination problem: courts must apply law consistently, develop doctrine, and resolve competing claims. BUT legislative override capacity creates asymmetric extraction — judicial reasoning can be invalidated through legislative amendment, requiring courts to absorb costs of doctrinal instability. Constrained by inability to override legislature, but also benefits from legislative legitimacy that shores up enforceability of judicial orders. Mixed coordination-extraction: courts coordinate the rule of law; legislatures extract interpretive supremacy.

perspectives.label: Elected Legislature
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 3: ELECTED LEGISLATURE (ROPE) — Primary beneficiary. Experiences the constraint as pure coordination: the democratic mandate justifies final say on fundamental law interpretation. Reflects the genuine coordination function of democratic accountability — majoritarian preference legitimately shapes law. Net beneficiary with arbitrage options: legislative majorities can substitute amendment for judicial override, can control the agenda, can leverage popular mandate. Minimal experienced extraction because legislatures are the constraint's primary architects.

perspectives.label: Constitutional Supermajority Requirements
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 4: SUPERMAJORITY GATEKEEPING (SCAFFOLD) — Organized procedural constraints (amending supermajorities, supermajority veto rights, minority representation in legislative structure) create temporary equilibrium that prevents pure majoritarian extraction. Supermajority rules function as a sunset mechanism: they remain operative only as long as the majority respects them. When parliamentary sovereignty is unconstrained (unicameral simple majority), the scaffold collapses. Classification reflects that this is a coordination solution with explicit enforceability limits — once the gate is breached, the mechanism ceases to function. The constraint has a natural terminus when legislature decides to abolish the supermajority rule itself.

perspectives.label: Institutional Designers and Framers
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 5: INSTITUTIONAL DESIGNERS (TANGLED ROPE) — Those with power to design or amend the constitutional structure see the constraint as a genuine coordination mechanism: legislative supremacy establishes clear authority chains and avoids deadlock between branches. But also extractive: designer interests shape which majority gets final say — small-nation framers favoring legislative supremacy; colonial designers, federal systems. Mobile exit options (can design alternative structures) but constrained by path dependence and legacy commitments. Experience mixed coordination-extraction because the design choice has path-dependent lock-in effects.

perspectives.label: Westminster Parliamentary Tradition
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 6: WESTMINSTER TRADITION AS INSTITUTIONAL THEATER (PITON) — The parliamentary supremacy doctrine persists as a formalized principle in Westminster-derived systems even where functional judicial independence has developed. Theater ratio reflects that actual constitutional practice (judicial review, rights protections, constitutional conventions) has substantially diverged from the formal doctrine that parliament is supreme. The doctrine is maintained as a legitimacy narrative rather than as a functioning mechanism of control. Courts operate as if they have real authority; legislatures exercise restraint; the supremacy principle remains untouched. Piton classification derives from the performative gap between stated doctrine and actual practice.

perspectives.label: Analytical Observer (Natural Law View)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 7: ANALYTICAL OBSERVER / NATURAL LAW VIEW (MOUNTAIN) — From a civilizational scale, democratic legitimacy itself may be seen as requiring final legislative authority: representation IS the coordinate principle of democracy; constraints on representative bodies are per se limits on democratic control. This perspective naturalizes parliamentary supremacy as inherent to democratic theory itself. However, the structural data contradicts this — the constraint has clear beneficiaries (legislatures, majoritarian coalitions) and victims (courts, minorities), indicating that it is a contingent institutional choice, not an inherent property of democracy.

omegas.question: Is judicial review of legislative acts compatible with parliamentary sovereignty, or does it necessarily foreclose the supremacy reading?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Constitutional text analysis (supremacy clause language); case law on standing, remedy availability, and enforcement; comparative study of how Westminster-derived systems handle legislative review
omegas.impact: If compatible: parliamentary sovereignty persists as a formal doctrine even where judicial review operates (piton classification confirmed). If incompatible: the supremacy reading forecloses judicial review, which many sibling readings (judicial_supremacy, popular_constitutionalism) explicitly protect.
omegas.description: Compatibility between judicial review and parliamentary sovereignty doctrine

omegas.question: Do procedurally-entrenched supermajority requirements genuinely constrain a subsequent legislature, or can an absolute majority abolish them at will (true parliamentary supremacy)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Constitutional law doctrine (entrenchment theory); empirical tracking of whether supermajority rules persist across constitutional crises; analysis of whether courts enforce entrenchment or defer to simple-majority amendment
omegas.impact: If genuinely binding: supermajority requirements constitute real structural limits (scaffold perspective confirmed). If abolishable: parliamentary supremacy is absolute, supermajority requirements are scaffolding that can be swept away (scaffold collapses to pure snare when majority chooses).
omegas.description: Whether supermajority requirements can be abolished by simple majority

omegas.question: At what degree of legislative override of established rights protections does the constraint cross from tangled_rope (mixed coordination-extraction) to snare (pure extraction)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Historical analysis of legislative override patterns (frequency, scope, affected rights categories); measurement of impact on political minorities; comparison with jurisdictions using alternative authority distributions
omegas.impact: If threshold is high: parliamentary sovereignty persists as a workable tangled_rope. If threshold is low: even moderate-frequency overrides reveal the constraint functions as a snare when legislative majorities are stable or ideologically unified.
omegas.description: Threshold at which legislative override patterns indicate snare rather than tangled_rope

omegas.question: Is parliamentary sovereignty a coherent reading of the basic law kernel, or does the coexistence of accepted judicial review and legislative supremacy represent an incoherent commitment system?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Doctrinal analysis of how courts and legislatures actually adjudicate conflicts; comparison with explicitly dual-authority systems (US constitutional model); evaluation of whether Westminster systems achieve stable equilibrium or oscillate between competing readings
omegas.impact: If coherent: the parliamentary sovereignty reading is valid and coexists with judicial review as a nested authority structure. If incoherent: the reading forecloses judicial supremacy within a single framework, and the constraint displays a forking dynamic where jurisdictions move toward one reading or the other.
omegas.description: Whether parliamentary sovereignty coexists coherently with judicial review or forecloses it

omegas.question: How do we measure whether rights minorities are actually victims of this constraint vs. beneficiaries of a rights-protecting legislature exercising sovereignty?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Longitudinal analysis of rights protection outcomes under different legislative majorities; measurement of rights violation patterns pre- and post-override; comparison with jurisdictions using judicial review as primary rights protection mechanism
omegas.impact: If minorities are systematically victimized: snare classification is appropriate. If minorities benefit from legislative protection (or neutral outcomes): beneficiary classification may be appropriate; victims designation may be descriptive only of potential rather than realized extraction.
omegas.description: Whether rights minorities are actual victims or only potential victims

commentary.kernel_context: This constraint instantiates the PARLIAMENTARY SOVEREIGNTY READING of the contested kernel 'basic_law_interpretive_authority' — the question of which institutional actor (legislature, courts, or the people) holds final say on what the constitution means. The parliamentary sovereignty reading answers: the elected legislature, grounded in democratic mandate and representative accountability. SIBLING READINGS (other constraints, not this one): (1) judicial_supremacy_reading — courts hold final interpretive authority based on legal expertise and rights protection; (2) popular_constitutionalism_reading — the people (through amendment, recall, plebiscite) hold final say, bypassing both legislative and judicial gatekeepers. Each reading instantiates a different ε, different beneficiary/victim structure, and different dominant constraint type. This reading treats the kernel's codification as fixed (the basic law text exists) and the authority grounding as legislative lineage (chain of constitutional transmission through elected bodies with electoral mandate). The drift state captures the gap between t0 reference frame (pure parliamentary supremacy) and t1 contemporary moment (judicial review and rights protections established in practice).
commentary.narrative_context: The parliamentary sovereignty reading holds that the elected legislature, as the sole institution directly accountable to voters and reflecting current majoritarian preference, must retain final interpretive authority over fundamental law. This reading prioritizes democratic legitimacy, representativeness, and responsiveness to changing public will over fixed constitutional principles or judicial guardianship. From this perspective, courts exist to apply law as legislatures define it; constitutional meaning follows majoritarian intent as expressed through democratic amendment procedures; rights protections depend on legislative good faith rather than judicial enforcement. The constraint exhibits tangled_rope structure: legislatures genuinely coordinate majoritarian preference-aggregation and democratic accountability (coordination function) while simultaneously extracting interpretive supremacy from courts and minorities who cannot override legislative constitutional readings (asymmetric extraction). The theater ratio (0.55) reflects that in Westminster-derived systems, the formal doctrine of parliamentary supremacy persists as legitimacy narrative even where judicial review has developed functional independence — courts frame themselves as deferring to legislative will while actually exercising independent judgment on constitutional boundaries.
key_agents: Elected Legislature: Primary beneficiary (institutional/arbitrage) — retains final interpretive authority, can override courts, sets constitutional agenda through amendment control, derives legitimacy from electoral mandate

Rights Minorities: Primary victim (powerless/trapped) — cannot exit the jurisdiction, vulnerable to majoritarian override of protections, lack institutional counterweight when legislative will conflicts with minority interests

Judicial Branch: Secondary victim and mixed actor (moderate/constrained) — must respect legislative interpretations as binding, but also benefits from legislative legitimacy that makes judicial orders enforceable; constrained by inability to override but coordinating the rule of law

Constitutional Supermajority Gatekeeping: Organized constraint (organized/constrained) — entrenchment requirements (if binding) function as temporary equilibrium preventing pure majoritarian extraction; collapses when majority abolishes supermajority rule

Institutional Designers/Framers: Powerful actors (powerful/mobile) — choose to grant parliament final authority; shape which majority gets interpretive power; experience constraint as coordination mechanism with path-dependent extraction

Westminster Tradition: Institutional narrative (institutional/arbitrage) — maintains parliamentary supremacy doctrine as formalized principle even where practice has diverged; operates as piton (performative theater masking functional independence)
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.52): Moderate-high. The legislature benefits structurally from retaining final authority over constitutional interpretation — this is genuine institutional extraction. The measurement reflects that the parliamentary sovereignty reading creates a stable benefit flow to legislatures and majoritarian coalitions over time. As the interval progresses (t0 → t100), extractiveness rises slightly (0.38 → 0.58) as judicial review becomes more functionally independent in practice while doctrine formally reaffirms supremacy — the gap between stated authority and actual constraints on legislatures grows, revealing hidden extraction. Suppression (0.48): Moderate. Rights minorities face significant barriers to protecting constitutional interests when legislatures can override judicial protections — cannot appeal to courts beyond legislative intent, cannot organize a blocking majority, face ballot constraints if legislative majorities are stable. Barriers are not absolute (exit to other jurisdictions is possible at high cost; constitutional amendment is available if supermajority emerges) but are real and substantial. Theater ratio (0.55): Moderate. Parliamentary supremacy operates partly as genuine authority mechanism (legislatures do hold de facto final say on constitutional meaning through amendment control and legislative override capacity) and partly as legitimacy theater (the doctrine persists formally even where courts exercise real independence, and majoritarian legislatures rarely encounter judicial constraints). The rise in theater_ratio over the interval (0.35 → 0.62) reflects increasing divorce between doctrine (supremacy) and practice (judicial review), suggesting the constraint is degrading toward piton status at the institutional scale.
commentary.perspectival_gap: This constraint produces a full perspectival range precisely because it instantiates a contested reading with structural tensions. Powerless minorities see snare (trapped, no exit, cannot override legislature). Courts see tangled_rope (coordination benefit of majoritarian legitimacy plus extraction cost of interpretive supremacy loss). Legislatures see rope (pure coordination benefit of having final say, reflecting democratic will). Supermajority gatekeeping sees scaffold (temporary coordination mechanism with explicit sunset when majority abolishes entrenchment). Institutional designers see tangled_rope (genuine coordination in establishing clear authority chains, extraction in the path-dependent lock-in of legislative power). Westminster tradition sees piton (formal doctrine of supremacy maintained as theater despite functional judicial independence). The analytical observer at civilizational scale risks seeing mountain (democracy naturally requires legislative supremacy), but the structural data reveals false summit — this is a contingent reading with clear winners and losers, not an inherent property of democracy itself.
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality derives from the structural position of each agent relative to the extraction flow. Legislatures (beneficiary + arbitrage exit) experience low d → negative χ (net beneficiaries). Rights minorities (victim + trapped exit) experience high d → high χ (maximum extraction). Courts (mixed + constrained exit) experience moderate d → moderate χ (real benefit from legislative legitimacy, real cost from interpretive subordination). Supermajority gatekeeping (organized + constrained) experiences lower-moderate d because organization partially offsets victimhood — coordinated minorities can defend the supermajority rule as long as it survives. Framers (beneficiary + mobile exit through design choice) experience low d but higher than pure beneficiaries because path dependence constrains future mobility. Westminster tradition (institutional/arbitrage) experiences moderate-low d because the piton status derives from theaters masking asymmetric extraction — the tradition benefits from supremacy doctrine but at the cost of incoherence.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The parliamentary sovereignty reading resolves mandatrophy by differentiating between genuine coordination (democratic accountability, majoritarian preference aggregation, clear authority chains — all real and valuable) and extraction asymmetries (supremacy over courts, dominance of minorities, path-dependent lock-in). The constraint is tangled_rope because BOTH elements are structurally present: legislatures really do coordinate majoritarian democracy, AND they really do extract interpretive authority from courts and minorities. The false summit perspective (mountain at analytical/civilizational scale) reveals that framers and theorists risk naturalizing this reading as inherent to democracy itself, when it is actually one of three live readings with different structural implications. The measurement drift (theater rising, extractiveness rising) indicates that over time the coordination benefit (legislative mandate legitimacy) may be overtaken by the extraction cost (judicial review constrained by supreme doctrine, minorities unprotected by independent courts). This is the classic pattern of a coordinate mechanism degrading into a piton: the coordination function persists as narrative while the extraction mechanism persists as institutional fact.

network.dual_formulation_note: The basic_law_interpretive_authority kernel has three structurally distinct constraint readings: (1) parliamentary_sovereignty_reading (this file) — legislature retains final say, ε=0.52, tangled_rope; (2) judicial_supremacy_reading — courts hold final authority, ε likely higher (>0.60), likely snare from legislative majority perspective; (3) popular_constitutionalism_reading — people hold final authority through amendment/recall/plebiscite, ε likely lower (<0.40), likely scaffold or rope. Each reading instantiates different beneficiary/victim structures, different measurements, and different classifications from the same base law kernel. They are linked as a constraint family because they share a common upstream kernel and represent different institutional resolutions of the same authority question. This reading (parliamentary sovereignty) influences the other two because parliamentary majorities can abolish alternative authority structures (judicial independence, amendment procedures) if they choose — the supremacy reading creates structural pressure on the others' survival.
